characteristics.oxidation: Minimal, with a smothering stage (men huang)
characteristics.harvestSeason: Early spring, a very short harvesting window

description.short: Delicate, sweet yellow tea made strictly from buds — a historic imperial tribute from the same sacred mountain as Mengding Ganlu
description.overview: Harvested on Mount Mengding, one of the cradle lands of tea cultivation, but crafted using yellow tea processing — featuring the smothered yellowing (men huang) stage that removes vegetal astringency.
description.leaf: Straight golden-yellow buds with delicate fine down
description.aroma: Mellow, sweet, with roasted nutty notes
description.taste: Delicate and sweet, devoid of green tea grassiness, with gentle toasted nut undertones
description.processing: Plucking buds only → gentle pan-firing fixation → smothering in damp cloth or paper (men huang) → light re-firing → final drying

history.origin: Mount Mengding was historically one of the earliest and most revered centers of imperial tribute tea in China, dating back to the Tang dynasty.
history.development: Alongside the green Mengding Ganlu, Huangya emerged as a premium tribute style from the same mountain, crafted using yellow tea smothered-oxidation methods.
history.modern: Today it is one of the few surviving yellow teas of Sichuan, handcrafted in strictly limited quantities.
interestingFacts: Mount Mengding supplied official imperial tribute tea ('gong cha') continuously across dynasties for well over a millennium until the fall of the Qing dynasty.
The smothered yellowing (men huang) step is the sole technical distinction between Mengding Huangya and green Mengding Ganlu from the same mountain, despite identical terroir and raw pluck.
